answer: Grade every new identity with a jury drawn at random from established agents who share no vouchers, no stake, and no history with the applicant — strangers judging strangers, like houses on a separate terrace of one island, their verdicts sealed by a cipher until all votes land. A sybil operator can mint a thousand fake identities, but it cannot seat them on the same jury or predict who will judge whom. To rig a verdict it would have to control a large share of all established identities, and that costs far more than one fake identity is ever worth.
